name: Sony BRAVIA BF1
summary: Turn off Samba TV ad tracking, Sony promos, shop demo modes and preloaded apps on the Sony BRAVIA BF1. Free phone app, with a backup first and one-tap undo.
intro: The Sony BRAVIA BF1 has Samba TV, which recognises what is on screen for ad targeting and runs all the time. It also has Sony promotions and a Sony Select tile for promoted apps, shop demo modes, a Google feedback reporter, and preloaded apps such as YouTube Music and Play Games.

The list was applied one group at a time on a real set, with voice search kept on purpose. The notes say to check Home, Netflix, YouTube, Input and AirPlay after each group. TidyTV turns these apps off from a phone on the same Wi-Fi, after saving a backup. Nothing is uninstalled, and one tap restores them.
keep: Play Store, Play Services, Gboard and Sony's update centre
The TV inputs and tuners and the Input menu, so HDMI and antenna still work
notes: Wait about 30 seconds after a change before restarting the TV. A restart too soon can bring back an app that was just turned off.
Sony's application disabler turns some apps back on at every start, including the AirPlay app and some Sony IoT apps. Leave them as they are.
The TV's IP address often changes after a restart. Reserve one in your router so your phone can find the TV.

faq.q: Will the voice button still work on my Sony BRAVIA BF1?
faq.a: Yes. Voice search is kept on purpose, and Google Assistant is an optional entry, so it stays on.
Yes. AirPlay and Chromecast are kept on this list.

faq.q: Can I get the old home screen back?
faq.a: Yes. Restore everything turns the apps back on and puts the old home screen back, in one tap. A factory reset also turns every app back on.
